findings.reason: The protected query is the canonical expert-interview solution: one CASE expression classifies every session during a grouped scan, a fixed four-row bin dimension preserves empty intervals, and a left join with COALESCE supplies zero totals. The structure and names are clear, the numeric sort key is not leaked, and no material improvement warrants a candidate.

The ascending thresholds 300, 600, and 900 seconds define mutually exclusive and exhaustive intervals, so every Sessions row contributes to exactly one count and exact-boundary values enter the interval beginning at that boundary. Driving the final join from all four labels produces every required bin even when an interval or the entire input is empty.

An independent Python oracle assigned durations directly to four counters without SQL or reuse of the reviewed CASE expression. It, the protected app query, exact immutable native query, an independently written conditional-aggregation query, and a correct slower correlated-aggregate control agreed on all eight visible cases and all three benchmark tiers.

Seed 1435 generated 5,000 deterministic schema-valid databases with zero through 180 rows, unique shuffled and noncontiguous session IDs, repeated durations, every side of the 300/600/900 boundaries, zero, long sessions through 100,000 seconds, and empty inputs. The protected query and independent conditional-aggregation control matched the direct Python oracle on every database; the correlated control also matched on 300 additional smaller randomized databases.

Across three real-test repetitions, the protected query passed all eight ordinary outputs, all three benchmark outputs, and scaling with extra growth exponent -0.01 through +0.01 and largest runtime ratio 1.00x through 1.02x. The independently correct O(n squared) correlated control passed every output but failed only scaling each time, with relative growth exponent +1.02 through +1.03 and largest ratio 24.79x through 25.92x.

The three existing benchmark tiers remain hidden and performance-only. Their positive unique sizes n=64, 256, and 1,024 span 16x, exercise classification across all four bins, and give the protected one-scan aggregation linear work while forcing the correlated control to rescan Sessions for every row. The slower control completes normally and fails only scaling, so benchmark.json was not edited.

The complete Approach now derives the 300/600/900-second boundaries, mutually exclusive classification, fixed-bin left join, zero filling, exact fourth-bin label, and optional constant-size ordering. It justifies O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary state and contrasts conditional UNION ALL, incomplete CASE-only grouping, and correlated rescans while covering boundaries, repeated durations, empty input, empty intervals, and unrestricted output order.

All eight ordinary correctness cases are visible samples or trials and use unordered-table validation because the source permits any result order. The single authenticated source example remains exact; added coverage includes zero and both sides of every boundary, lower bounds, noncontiguous IDs, first-only and middle-only populations, repeated durations, empty Sessions, long sessions, zero-count bins, and deliberately reordered expected rows.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode database problem 1435 and SQL as the active language. Reviewed artifacts preserve the unique session_id fact, duration-in-seconds meaning, exact four labels and half-open boundaries, two-column output, and unrestricted result order. The authenticated source has no separate constraints, hints, notes, images, diagrams, or follow-up section.

The protected app and immutable native SQL sources are byte-identical and remain bound to verified submission 2069089789. Both source files and submission.json remain unchanged, their one-scan classification and fixed-bin join are exactly aligned, and no candidate exists.

A fresh authenticated Premium review confirmed the Sessions schema, duration units, four interval semantics and exact output labels, one exact example with explanation, three logical source tables, and the absence of every separate ancillary section. source_fidelity.json binds the four modular Reference files to live-content SHA-256 0757a06c4ad69dd45f703d71ea00730745ad42ec9bd1fbe2adac43590f267d53 and validates without errors.
